newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian parties sign deal on EU entry.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian parties sign deal on EU entry.

text.p: Leaders of Slovenia's parliamentary parties signed a cross-party agreement on Friday that enables them to coordinate the country's efforts to join the European Union as soon as possible.
"This agreement is very important for us -- I think the way to European integration is now open," Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek told a news conference after signing the agreement.
The parties said in the agreement that they are willing to liberalise the Alpine republic's real estate market in line with the EU association treaty.

The Constitutional Court last month ordered parliament to change the country's legislation to allow foreigners to buy land in line with EU standards, and only then would it ratify the EU association agreement, signed a year ago.
Drnovsek said he expected the amendment to the constitution to take place by July 15 and ratification of the association agreement to follow swiftly.

The European Commission has said that speedy ratification of the association agreement was a precondition for Slovenia to join the first round of the EU's expansion. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
